correctness.rationale: The proof first characterizes diagonal surjectivity via maximal ideals of the polynomial ring and the Chinese remainder theorem. It classifies every cover two-by-two subalgebra surjecting to Fq×Fq: its off-diagonal kernel either vanishes, forcing all generator cover coordinates proportional to the diagonal difference through one conjugating scalar, or is all of Fq, giving the full two-by-two triangular ring. Semisimple splitting and conjugacy apply because the base prime field is perfect and the finite diagonal quotient is separable; conjugation and products of all cover units recover the whole incidence algebra. This gives necessary and sufficient independent tests and the exact product formula. The standalone checker independently closes all generated subrings in seven exhaustive finite-field/poset instances and agrees with the prediction. Finite checks alone cannot establish the infinite theorem; that role is played by the proof.

originality.rationale: The first source counts generation after all coefficient scalar matrices are included, whereas this result counts unital ring generation without those scalars; the two probabilities demonstrably differ over nonprime fields. The second source already supplies the Frobenius orbit number for the diagonal étale quotient and is credited. Neither inspected paper supplies the needed local-to-global prime-field radical lifting and factorized ring generation formula for arbitrary incidence posets. Searches for aliases and stronger finite-algebra statements did not find an identical or dominating formula. Potential implicit earlier coverage remains a named risk; no uniqueness is asserted.
residual_risks: An implicit prime-field ring statement might exist in the inaccessible full text of Kolegov (2023) or Kolegov–Markova (2018/2019).
An independently discovered, unindexed equivalent factorization could exist; search absence is not mathematical proof of uniqueness.
Wedderburn–Malcev is invoked as a standard structure theorem, not independently formalized.

value.rationale: The unassisted random ring generation probability is a natural, presently distinct invariant from the scalar-assisted incidence-algebra probability, with direct implications for generating finite rings from actual matrix tuples. The finding supplies its complete exact formula for every finite poset, a sharp positive generator threshold, and a poset-independent Galois penalty separating finite-field extension and radical obstructions. The explicit F4 two-vertex count halves the scalar-assisted probability, showing mathematical substance beyond relabeling the known formula. The local cover splitting theorem is structural and supports comparisons across arbitrary Hasse diagrams; no unsupported downstream theorem is asserted.
